<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD defines sources for both x86_64 and aarch64 architectures, pointing to `.deb` packages hosted on `cdn-zcode.z.ai`, which appears to be the official domain for the ZCode application. The `source` arrays use standard URL syntax and include proper checksums via `sha256sums`, so the integrity of the downloaded binaries will be verified during the build process. There are no command substitutions, unquoted variables, or inline execution in the `source` array that could lead to arbitrary code execution during download.

The PKGBUILD contains no `pkgver()` function, so version computation is not dynamic. The top-level scope consists only of static variable assignments. No code is executed during sourcing beyond simple string and array assignments. The `package()` function is irrelevant for this gate, as it is not run under `--noprepare --nobuild --nodeps`. Therefore, sourcing the PKGBUILD and downloading the sources poses no risk of unintended or malicious execution.

While the sources are prebuilt `.deb` binaries (which limits auditability of the final binary contents), that is not a concern for this narrow gate, which only evaluates whether fetching and parsing the PKGBUILD is safe. The use of `sha256sums` instead of `SKIP` further strengthens trust in the source integrity.
</details>
